hospitals.peds_trauma_level: Level I pediatric trauma center (ACS verified, only one in South Carolina)
hospitals.description: MUSC Shawn Jenkins Children's Hospital is the flagship pediatric hospital for the Medical University of South Carolina and the state's main referral center for complex care in children. The building opened in February 2020 on the downtown Charleston medical district next to MUSC's adult hospital and also houses the Pearl Tourville Women's Pavilion. It holds the state's only ACS verified Level I pediatric trauma center and its only pediatric burn program, a Level IV NICU, and a 24/7 intensivist staffed PICU backed by the MEDUCARE pediatric flight team. Its heart program is nationally prominent, ranking in the top five in U.S. News. The peninsula campus sits a short walk from downtown Charleston's historic district.
highlights: Only U.S. News ranked children's hospital in SC: six specialties in the national top 50 for 2025-26, cardiology and heart surgery No. 4
Only ACS Level I pediatric trauma center and only pediatric burn center in South Carolina
Level IV NICU, largest in the state (82 to 89 beds reported)
28-bed PICU with in-house intensivist 24/7, 10-bed intermediate care, pediatric ECMO
MEDUCARE pediatric flight team by helicopter, plane, or ambulance statewide
250 licensed beds, all private rooms, opened February 2020
ANCC Magnet (MUSC)
hospitals.notes: Shares the downtown MUSC campus with MUSC Health University Medical Center (171 Ashley Ave, 865 licensed beds, Magnet), which holds the adult Level I trauma designation; no separate adult record was created. Bed and unit counts vary by source: MUSC critical care page says 28 PICU beds, a 2026 MUSC faculty posting says 25 PICU and 89 NICU beds, the 2019 MUSC review says the NICU grew from 66 to 82 beds. The MUSC Division of Pediatric Child Abuse alone lists seven APPs. Downtown peninsula parking and traffic are real commute factors; many staff live in Mount Pleasant, West Ashley, James Island or Summerville.

hospitals.description: Prisma Health Children's Hospital-Midlands is the pediatric hospital on the Prisma Health Richland campus just north of downtown Columbia, the main children's referral center for the 16-county Midlands region. Richland is the designated Regional Perinatal Center for the Midlands, so the NICU takes infants of any gestational age and birth weight, and the campus carries the area's only Level II pediatric trauma designation. A 16-bed PICU staffed by a group of pediatric intensivists sees more than 900 admissions a year and also runs a large procedural sedation service. A dedicated children's emergency room and an outpatient specialty center sit on the same medical park, and USC School of Medicine residents train here.
highlights: One of four children's hospitals in South Carolina (SC Children's Hospital Collaborative member)
Regional Perinatal Center (Level III) for the 16-county Midlands region
16-bed PICU with over 900 admissions per year and resident coverage at all times
Level II pediatric trauma center on a Level I adult trauma campus
Dedicated children's emergency room on the Richland campus
Primary pediatric teaching site for University of South Carolina School of Medicine
hospitals.notes: beds is the parent Richland Hospital count (641 per Prisma, 649 licensed per Wikipedia); the children's hospital's own bed count was not found. nicu_level 3 reflects the SC DPH Regional Perinatal Center Level III designation; AAP level not confirmed. wikipedia_title points to the parent Richland article because the children's hospital has no article. Children's ER is listed at 5 Richland Medical Park Dr. Columbia commuters often live in Lexington, Irmo, Blythewood or Forest Acres.

hospitals.description: Prisma Health Children's Hospital-Upstate is the children's hospital inside Greenville Memorial Hospital, the largest hospital in the Prisma Health system and the main tertiary center for the South Carolina Upstate. It is one of the state's four children's hospitals and serves as a regional perinatal center for low birth weight infants, with a NICU, a PICU, a dedicated pediatric emergency department and a general pediatrics floor on the fifth floor. The USC School of Medicine Greenville campus sits on the same Grove Road campus, so residents and students are part of daily care. Greenville itself is a fast growing small city with a walkable downtown and quick access to the Blue Ridge foothills.
highlights: One of four children's hospitals in South Carolina (SC Children's Hospital Collaborative member)
Inside 814-bed Greenville Memorial Hospital, Prisma Health's largest campus
Regional perinatal center for low birth weight infants per the SC Children's Hospital Collaborative
Dedicated children's emergency room and PICU
USC School of Medicine Greenville located on campus
Prisma Health Upstate mother/baby unit pioneered the MAiN newborn care model
hospitals.notes: beds is the parent Greenville Memorial count (814 per Wikipedia; the Wikipedia hospital list says 864). Children's bed count, PICU bed count, NICU AAP level and pediatric trauma level were not confirmed because prismahealth.org and prismahealthchildrens.org were blocked this session; nicu_level 3 is based on the regional perinatal center role. Commuter towns include Simpsonville, Mauldin, Greer, Travelers Rest and Easley.

hospitals.description: McLeod Children's Hospital is the pediatric service of McLeod Regional Medical Center in downtown Florence, the hub of a 7-hospital not-for-profit system that covers the Pee Dee region of northeastern South Carolina. It runs the only pediatric intensive care unit in the region, caring for patients up to age 18, and a Level III NICU that is one of seven in the state, with 40 NICU beds in the regional medical center. The parent hospital is a Level II trauma center with a pediatric trauma bay in its emergency department and three helipads. It is one of the state's four recognized children's hospitals and a regional perinatal center, drawing families from rural counties across the Pee Dee.
highlights: One of four children's hospitals in South Carolina (SC Children's Hospital Collaborative member)
Only PICU in the Pee Dee region, ages up to 18
Level III NICU, one of seven in SC; 40 NICU beds at McLeod Regional
Parent hospital is a 461-bed Level II trauma center with a pediatric trauma bay and three helipads
Regional perinatal center serving a largely rural, high Medicaid population
hospitals.notes: beds is the parent McLeod Regional Medical Center (461 licensed per Wikipedia McLeod Health article; the Wikipedia hospital list says 517). teaching is set because the SC Children's Hospital Collaborative describes all four children's hospitals as primary training sites for public medical schools; the specific school was not confirmed. Google Places lists a McLeod Regional Medical Center Pediatric Intensive Care Unit at the same address. Florence is about 70 miles from Myrtle Beach and 80 miles from Columbia. MUSC Health Florence Medical Center is a competitor across town.

hospitals.description: Grand Strand Medical Center is the HCA Healthcare flagship on the Grand Strand, a 403-bed regional hospital on 82nd Parkway in north Myrtle Beach. It is the region's Level I adult trauma center and a Level II pediatric trauma center, and it has a pediatric intensive care unit, which makes it the main acute pediatric referral point along the coast between Wilmington and Charleston. A 2014 expansion added pediatric, medical surgical and ICU capacity, and Galen College of Nursing opened a campus at the hospital in 2022. The hospital serves a large year-round population plus heavy summer tourist volume.
highlights: Level I adult trauma center and Level II pediatric trauma center
Has a PICU, rare for a community setting on the coast
403 beds; comprehensive stroke center; cardiac surgery and neurosurgery
2014 expansion enhanced pediatrics

hospitals.description: Summerville Medical Center is an HCA hospital in the fast growing Summerville suburb northwest of Charleston and part of the Trident Health market with Trident Medical Center. Despite its modest size it runs a 6-bed PICU with two observation beds, an inpatient pediatric floor and a Level III NICU, with pediatric intensivists from Pediatrix in house during the day. The maternity program is busy at about 2,800 births a year, and pediatric surgery and pediatric GI surgery provide onsite backup. Complex cases transfer to a quaternary center in Charleston about 45 minutes away.
highlights: 6-bed PICU plus 2 observation beds, 85 PICU admissions in 2024
Level III NICU
About 2,800 births per year

Pediatric intensivist coverage by Pediatrix Medical Group
